craft_claim: Reverent awe requires the compelling (fascinans) alongside the daunting; when the object is rendered as pure power that subjugates, threat-based awe dominates and the voice becomes grim or horrific, not reverent.

supporting_evidence.location: JPSP, DOI 10.1037/pspp0000120, studies distinguishing threat-based awe
supporting_evidence.note: Gordon et al. distinguish a threat-based variant of awe associated with fear, reduced sense of control, and submission, and show it is not reliably prosocial - unlike positive awe.

supporting_evidence.location: The Idea of the Holy, chs. III-IV (mysterium tremendum et fascinans)
supporting_evidence.note: Otto holds tremendum and fascinans together; reverence is the dual response, so terror without attraction is a deformation.

scope: Boundary rule against tone-grim and horror engines; applies wherever a narrator faces overwhelming power.
exceptions: Horror and tragic forms may deliberately stage threat-awe as a temporary state before or without the reverent resolution.
